objective: Settle by two-arm measurement whether the adjoint matrix reordering lever this lab has requested in 257 archived runs does anything at all, by reading the ordering back out of the linear solver itself rather than out of the wrapper's own echo
rationale: The dead lever audit measured the following over 1,635 archived log files: 386 print the requested reordering, 257 of those request the reverse Cuthill McKee ordering, 8 carry a readback from the linear solver naming the ordering actually built, and the intersection of the last two is zero. So the lever has activity proof in none of the runs that request it, while the same ordering is separately proven effective five times elsewhere, which is exactly the configuration that makes an unproven lever look settled. The audit also found the mechanism that would let it be silently dead: the wrapper prints its reordering, overlap and fill level parameters regardless of which preconditioner was actually constructed, demonstrated on a run whose own solver dump shows an algebraic multigrid preconditioner while the wrapper prints parameters belonging to two preconditioners the run never built. That is the configured-is-not-active defect in its structural form, and it is the lesson this lab cites more than any other, with 104 citations across the corpus, and the one it has least mechanised. The class matters more than the case: 257 runs inherit whatever the answer is, and any future conclusion that cites this lever inherits it too. Two arms of an existing configuration settle it, and no new case, mesh or geometry is involved
gate: Two arms of the archived rung-4 hump adjoint configuration, run to iteration 10 only, with -ksp_view enabled. Arm A requests jacMatReOrdering natural; arm B requests rcm. Everything else is byte-identical between the arms and matches the archived dictionaries by sha256, asserted before launch. PASS (the lever is ACTIVE) if the 'matrix ordering:' line in the PETSc -ksp_view dump differs between the arms and matches what each arm requested. FAIL (the lever is DEAD in this build) if the two dumps report the same ordering. NO VERDICT, per docket B2, if the -ksp_view dump does not contain a matrix ordering line at all in either arm -- that is a statement about what this build exposes, and it is reported as such rather than defaulted to either side. IDENTITY TEST, per Verification Charter 2a. Q1, what makes this FAIL: two identical ordering readbacks. Q2, could a wrong treatment still pass? A gate phrased as 'did the arm converge' or 'did the wrapper print rcm' passes with the lever completely dead -- the wrapper's own print is the surface the audit demonstrated lying -- which is precisely why neither is gated here and the PETSc dump is. Two arms rather than one because a single natural arm cannot discriminate against PETSc's own default, which may also be natural. SECONDARY, reported and not gated: the KSP iteration count at iteration 10 in each arm. If the readbacks differ but the iteration counts are identical to the digit, the lever is active and inert, which is a different and equally useful answer. EXTERNAL REFERENT, per Verification Charter 6a: PETSc's own -ksp_view self-report on the object it built. This is external to the DAFoam wrapper, which is the surface under suspicion, and it is NOT external to PETSc, which is stated rather than glossed -- there is no third party here who can tell us what PETSc built.
cost_basis: Eight core minutes, from measured wall time in the archived hump logs rather than by analogy. Two arms at four ranks, roughly one minute each, because the adjoint's cost out to iteration 10 is dominated by the coloring and assembly phase measured at about 112 seconds in the archived rung-4 adjoint log, not by the ten iterations themselves. Cross check on the same box and the same solver family: the rung-2 comparison dump that killed the diagonal spread hypothesis cost 6.2 core minutes for a two-configuration diagnostic of the same shape. Basis gross, on the charter's binding unit of wall seconds times ranks divided by sixty. This lab's forecasts score zero of three within twenty percent and sixteen closed items recorded no actual cost at all, so the honest confidence statement is that eight is a measured floor and the coloring phase is the term that could move it; the item carries a hard stop at iteration 10 in each arm so an overrun is bounded by construction rather than by intention
expected_knowledge_gain: One measurement retires or confirms a lever across 257 archived runs at once, which is the only reason to buy it rather than caveating each conclusion that cites it. If the lever is dead, every ordering claim resting on the wrapper's echo is void and the wrapper needs an effective value echo, which the defect candidate record already recommends on separate override grounds and which this would establish on preconditioner-type grounds with no override present. If the lever is active, the audit's headline unproven entry closes and the same two-arm shape becomes the cheap template for the other configured-is-not-active questions in the adjoint stack. The secondary iteration count answers a second question for free: whether an ordering that is genuinely applied changes anything measurable on this operator, whose condition number the elimination table already puts near ten to the eleventh and insensitive to every preconditioner parameter this build exposes
hard_criterion_note: No new family and no new case: two arms of a configuration already on the record, run to iteration 10, whose entire purpose is to check whether an instrument reports what it claims. Charter 3 section 3 names this purpose explicitly and section 9 requires it labelled at launch, which this does

launch_prompt: Reordering lever two-arm measurement. Budget 8 core-min HARD, split evenly, hard stop at KSP iteration 10 in each arm. Step 1, zero compute: locate the archived rung-4 hump adjoint configuration, take sha256 of every dictionary, and record them in the pre-registration BEFORE launching. State in writing that the two arms differ in exactly one entry, jacMatReOrdering, and prove it with a diff in the record. Step 2: arm A with jacMatReOrdering natural and -ksp_view on. Step 3: arm B with rcm, identical otherwise. Step 4: extract the 'matrix ordering:' line from each PETSc dump and apply the three-valued verdict in the gate field. If neither dump carries an ordering line, the verdict is NO VERDICT and you report that, you do NOT substitute the wrapper's printInfo line -- that line is the thing under test. Report the iteration-10 KSP counts as a secondary, ungated observation. setsid, launch_solve.sh registered, collector armed, nothing left running. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/ with frame, filter and commit on every count; update docket D10; if the verdict is FAIL, do NOT sweep the 257 runs yourself -- file the sweep as its own item, because a 257-run re-reading is not this 8 core-min purchase.
